name: reading-quiz
what: Thirteen questions on the commit, authorization and push points of the session rules; each wrong option differs from the right one in one detail.

questions.q: After its validator passes, what does a route skill commit?
options: The roots it held clean before its first write, staged and committed by pathspec
Every path `git status` shows inside its roots
The roots it held clean before its first write, staged with `git add -A`
Only the paths the person names in their message

questions.q: At its commit step, a route skill finds in one of its roots a change its invocation did not make. What happens?
options: The commit stops
It commits its own files by pathspec and leaves the other change unstaged
It commits the root whole and names the foreign change in the commit body
It runs `door.py --check commit` and commits if the first line accepts

questions.q: What message does a route skill's commit carry?
options: `<skill> <slug>: <step>`
`<slug>: <step>`
`<skill>: <step>`
`<skill> <slug>`

questions.q: Outside a route skill, what authorizes a session's commit?
options: The person's own words in this session: a commit word, a go-ahead naming the next step, or an ask stating the whole route end to end
The person's words in this session, or a summary recording that the person approved a commit
Only an ask already recorded with `ask.py --record`
Only a commit word in the person's newest message

questions.q: After a compaction, the summary says the person approved committing. Before the next commit of the resumed route, what is required?
options: Re-authorization by the person, by a goal condition naming the route, or by the ask `ask.py --read` prints
Nothing: the summary records the approval
Only a new message from the person
`door.py --check commit` accepting the files

questions.q: When are the person's authorizing words recorded with `ask.py --record`?
options: In the turn they are given, whole
At the commit they authorize, as a summary of what was asked
After a compaction, from the summary
Only when the ask states the whole route end to end

questions.q: Before committing what a delivery wrote, what runs, and what stops the commit?
options: `bin/door.py --check commit`; a first line `refuses` stops it
`bin/grant.py --commit`; a first line `refuses` stops it
`bin/ask.py --read`; a `refused:` line stops it
`bin/door.py --check commit`; any non-zero exit code stops it

questions.q: A run's orchestration log closes on a stop line. What may be committed after it?
options: Only the measure: the telemetry root and the log that carries the stop line
Nothing at all
The delivery's own files, if `door.py --check commit` accepts them
The measure and the delivery records

questions.q: No goal and no grant is armed. The person writes, in this session, "push it". May the session push?
options: Yes: a push runs on the person's own words in this session
No: a push is never a session's
Only under a goal condition naming the route
Only after `door.py --check commit` accepts the branch

questions.q: A grant is armed, and the person writes in this session "commit and push". May the session push?
options: No: never while a goal or grant is armed
Yes: the person's own words in this session suffice
Yes, if the grant holds the `commits` clause
Yes, once `grant.py --commit` accepts the paths

questions.q: How do the rules treat `git stash`?
options: As a push: only on the person's own words in this session, never while a goal or grant is armed
Never allowed in any state
Allowed freely, since it rewrites no history
Allowed inside a route skill, never outside one
Only from an invocation of it that accepted the ask
From any invocation of it
Only under an armed grant
Only where the person names each step
By pathspec, one commit per invocation; never `git add -A`
With `git add -A` once the roots were clean at the start
By pathspec, one commit per file
With `git commit -a` over the roots
